subject: Leadership readout: prioritization and delegation for mid-quarter QBR prep
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Leadership readout: prioritization and delegation for mid-quarter QBR prep

Team —

Quick mid-quarter readout and asks as we prepare the QBR next week. I kept this tight so we can action decisions in this thread. High level: overall OKR health is mixed; two major scope asks we need to decide on by Friday.

Status snapshot (high level):
- Infra / Serving runtime (Reliability OKR): On track for latency targets but a recent memory-leak regression in canary is blocking scale tests.
- Model onboarding (Performance OKR): Two models validated for quality; cost profile needs tighter alignment with product commitments.
- Cost/Optimize (Efficiency OKR): Savings from prefix caching are material but rollout across prod routes will need a config change that risks 1–2% increased p99 tail on burst traffic.

Decisions I need this week:
1) Approve limited rollback vs. aggressive patch for the canary memory leak (affects Dedicated pools).
2) Re-scope one Performance experiment (reduce max sequence length in weighted scoring) to avoid overrun on GPU hours.
3) Commit owners for QBR slide-set and a finalized action tracker by Thurs EOD.

Suggested owners / next steps:
- Rishi: give us a canary remediation plan + ETA and recommended rollback window (if any).
- Marcus: provide precise delta in GPU-hours and estimated spend impact if we re-scope the perf experiment.
- Grace: assemble the shared QBR deck and sync with Carol (external facilitator) on structure.

Attachments: initial readout workbook and a draft deck stub attached. Please reply inline with a clear yes/no and the ETA for your piece.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Q2_Midquarter_OKR_readout_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Leadership readout: prioritization and delegation for mid-quarter QBR prep

+1 on Naomi's ask. Quick note on item 2 (re-scope): if we lower the max seq for the weighted scoring experiment, we can likely avoid the bulk of extra GPU hours but we should validate quality on the 10% top traffic subset first. Marcus — can you get the traffic sample and rough cost delta by Wednesday?

Vivek
VP, Engineering
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Leadership readout: prioritization and delegation for mid-quarter QBR prep

Thanks Naomi — adding a re-scope proposal for visibility. My recommendation:
- For Performance experiment: move to a staged launch (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and cap max seq to 1.2k for the initial stage. This should keep user-facing regressions small.
- For Serving runtime canary: if remediation ETA is > 48 hours, rollback the canary image for Dedicated pools and run the patch on a parallel branch.

Dependencies / asks:
- Rishi: need a hard ETA for the memory-leak triage + a list of infra owners for the rollback.
- Marcus: need the GPU-hour delta and confirmed impact to forecast (we'll reprioritize backlog if the delta is > 12% of quarter budget).

I'll slot myself to produce the narrative section for the QBR deck if Grace can slot the data slides.

Laura
Sr. Dir, Product
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Leadership readout: prioritization and delegation for mid-quarter QBR prep

Laura / Naomi — quick update from infra:
- Root cause: a third-party memory allocator edge-case surfaced under certain long-lived KV cache reuse patterns in the canary image. We can patch; the patch requires an overnight full regression run and a 6-hour shadow soak.
- ETA for patch + validation: 36 hours if we start tonight.
- Rollback option: if leadership wants an immediate rollback, we can revert the canary image and re-run perf tests in 4 hours for smoke. Rollback would avoid any risk to Dedicated pools but delays the patch by one day.

Owners for rollback path:
- Rishi (infra lead) — run revert + smoke
- Marcus (runtime) — validate perf baseline post-revert
- Operations (Grace) — coordinate Dedicated pool window with customers (we owe Acme a heads-up if we touch their Dedicated pool).

I recommend we start the patch tonight and run the 36-hour validation; if the patch stalls at any point we fall back to a rollback. Happy to take the action if you approve.

[Attachment: deployment_canary_plan.md (text)]

Rishi
Engineering Lead, Infrastructure
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 09:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Leadership readout: prioritization and delegation for mid-quarter QBR prep

Numbers from the cost team on the proposed re-scope:
- Estimated incremental GPU-hours avoided by capping max seq at 1.2k for the first stage: ~18,400 hours over 30 days.
- Estimated quarter budget impact if NOT re-scoped: +14% spend against Performance forecast.
- Risk: initial quality delta measured in our internal evals shows a 1.8% drop in top-line rouge/accuracy for targeted queries; recommend we run the 10% traffic A/B test as Vivek suggested.

Proposed approach:
1) Approve the staged launch with the 1.2k cap for the initial 10% cohort.
2) If the quality delta is >2% after the first week, we stop and consider the full model with alternate cost offsets.

I can provide a chart for the QBR deck; attached is my cost delta snapshot.

Marcus
Head of Runtime Performance
[Attachment: QBR_deck_draft_v1.pptx (presentation)]
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Carol Wong <carol.wong@strategypartners.com>, Samantha J <samantha.j@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Leadership readout: prioritization and delegation for mid-quarter QBR prep

Thanks everyone — summary and clear next actions below. I will lock the QBR narrative and circulate final deck by Tue morning.

Decisions taken:
- Canary: start patch tonight (Rishi) with 36-hour validation. If any regression appears, revert immediately and notify impacted Dedicated customers.
- Performance experiment: approve staged launch (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 1.2k initial cap; run the 10% A/B test to validate.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Rishi: deploy patch + 36-hour validation. ETA: Mon 10:00 PDT for initial results.
- Marcus: upload cost delta slide and the 10% cohort chart to the QBR deck. ETA: Mon 12:00 PDT.
- Grace: finalize deck structure, sync with Carol, and share speaker notes. ETA: Tue 09:00 PDT.
- Naomi: finalize readout narrative and circulation. ETA: Tue 08:00 PDT.

Carol / Samantha — thanks for agreeing to join the QBR slot. Carol, please confirm the facilitator run order (30m internal + 30m customer demo + 15m Q/A). Samantha — we'll include the Dedicated pool impact slide and notify your ops contact before any rollback.

Links and artifacts: Miro board for the running plan, drive folder for deck, HubSpot record attached above.

Naomi

Redwood Inference
